week_quote: When we pause together, love has time to speak.

sections.title: Shared Silence
sections.tagline: One minute of simply being - no goal, no sound, just calm.
body: Sit together in a circle, holding hands lightly or touching shoulders.
Close your eyes and just breathe together for a minute.
Feel the quiet air you all share.
sections.note: Even Alio manages stillness here… impressive.

sections.title: The Compliment Toss
sections.tagline: Trust grows when we throw kindness, not criticism.
body: Stand in a circle.
The person whose name starts closest to the end of the alphabet pretends to hold an invisible ball.
They ‘throw’ it gently to someone while saying one specific compliment to this person.
The receiver catches it saying: ‘Thank you!’
Then throws to someone else.
Continue until everyone has received at least one compliment or longer if you wish.
sections.note: Throw compliments softly, we’re spreading joy, not bruises.

sections.title: One True Word
sections.tagline: Truth, even in one word, is the beginning of trust.
body: Each person says one word
that honestly describes
how they feel right now.
sections.note: One honest word - and no, ‘fine’ doesn’t count.

sections.title: Gentle Breath Flow
sections.tagline: One breath, many bodies - the same calm flowing through all.
body: Everyone breathes in for 4 counts, out for 6, for one minute.
Feel the room breathing as one.
sections.note: Slow breaths: the one thing I never speed up.

sections.title: Family Sound Symphony
sections.tagline: Harmony happens when every voice matters.
body: The person whose birthday comes next starts by making one short sound (like bop! or ding!).
Go clockwise, the next person repeats the first sound and adds a different sound. Keep going around until everyone has layered in. You can go for more rounds to create a longer symphony.
Once you are ready, perform your ‘sound symphony’ together a few times in unison.
sections.note: Add your sound proudly, even if it’s slightly questionable.

sections.title: What I Love About Being Us
sections.tagline: When we remember what we love about ‘us,’ we reconnect to what truly matters.
body: Each person completes the sentence:
One thing I love about being in this family is…
sections.note: Say it with heart, dramatic speeches optional but appreciated.

sections.title: Still Hands
sections.tagline: Each touch is a reminder: peace can travel from one heart to another.
body: Place one hand on your own heart and the other on the shoulder of the person next to you.
Breathe slowly for one minute and feel the calm spreading.
sections.note: I’m holding very still... but my fingers are secretly planning a tickle attack.

sections.title: Freeze Family
sections.tagline: Shared imagination sparks shared joy.
body: The youngest person starts by shouting a word (e.g. hug, snow, kiss, Christmas Tree).
Everyone instantly freezes in a matching pose for 3 seconds. The caller chooses the person who shouts next word.
Play for a few rounds.
For 2 people: one freezes in a pose and the second one guesses what it is.
sections.note: The slower you freeze, the weirder you look. Trust me.

sections.title: My Favorite Moment Today
sections.tagline: Even ordinary moments can be extraordinary when noticed.
body: Everyone shares
one moment they enjoyed today.
Something that felt good.
sections.note: Yes, snacks can be a valid favorite moment.

sections.title: Flame Focus
sections.tagline: Even the smallest light shines brighter when seen together.
body: Sit close and gaze softly at a small flame or light.
Notice every flicker and breathe with it.
sections.note: Let your eyes rest - the flame can handle the work.

sections.title: Echo Wave
sections.tagline: Creativity unites faster than perfection.
body: The person who has the longest hair begins by saying in a normal voice one joyful sentence (I love Christmas! I wait for Santa Clause).
Going anticlockwise, each person must repeat the sentence using a different tone: robot tone, tiny-baby tone, duck tone, opera singer tone, old-lady tone, superhero tone…
Once a full circle is completed, a person on the right of the starter picks a new sentence and you do another round.
No tone is allowed to repeat in any round.
sections.note: Pick a voice you won’t regret hearing back immediately.

sections.title: The Color of My
sections.tagline: Colors give feelings a simple, creative shape.
body: Each person chooses a color that describes their day and says it aloud.
sections.note: Any color counts - even the one you invented five seconds ago.

sections.title: Listening to Quiet
sections.tagline: One minute of pure awareness of space and sound.
body: Close your eyes.
Notice three layers of sound:
near, far, and subtle.
sections.note: Shhh… even my thoughts soften for this one.

sections.title: Human Clock
sections.tagline: Coordination becomes teamwork when every person stays alert.
body: Everyone sits in a circle. The tallest person says ‘1’ and points at someone to continue. Whoever is pointed at says ‘2’ and points to the next person for ‘3’ and so on until ‘12’. If anyone makes mistake you reset and start over. Now repeat the whole clock faster and again backward from 12 to 1. You can change the target number to the higher one.

Final Advanced Round You need to count to 12 (or higher number) as a group without pre-agreeing who starts and who says next number. You just observe others and try not to say next number simultaneously with another person. If it happens you start over. This version is also perfect it there are only 2 people participating.
sections.note: Be sharp - this clock doesn’t accept delays.

sections.title: The Sound I Love at Home
sections.tagline: Home is built from sounds that make us feel safe.
body: Everyone names one comforting sound they love hearing at home.
sections.note: The sound of the WiFi connecting or frigde opening? Please don’t make me choose!

sections.title: Breathing Circle
sections.tagline: When we breathe together, we remember - we are one living rhythm
body: Everyone sits in a loose circle, hands on their own knees or joined lightly.
Imagine one shared breath moving gently through all of you like a soft wave.
sections.note: Breathe together… it’s teamwork in its quietest form.

sections.title: Family Balance Flow
sections.tagline: Balance grows when we share direction.
body: Everyone stands shoulder-to-shoulder in a row. Round 1 The youngest person becomes the leader and also participates in a game. They call simple directions choosing from below moves: lean forward, lean back, lean left, lean right. Everyone follows at the same pace. The goal is to reach at least 10 group moves without any mistake. Round 2 The next person in age order leads by calling tiny, synchronized steps: step forward, step backward, step right or step left. Everyone moves together until you reach at least 15 moves without any mistake. Final Round The oldest person uses mixed moves: leaning, single or multiple steps in a various pace. Play as long as you wish.
sections.note: Lean gracefully - dramatic falling is for later.

sections.title: A Word of Calm
sections.tagline: When we share calming words, we learn how to bring peace to ourselves and others.
body: Each person shares specific expressions they love to hear from a family members that help them calm down.
sections.note: Choose a word that lands like a feather, not like a thunderbolt.

sections.title: Weight of Peace
sections.tagline: Peace grows when we let ourselves be held , by the earth, by each other.
body: Sit or lie near each other. Let your body rest completely. Feel the floor supporting all of you equally - one safe ground beneath many hearts.
sections.note: I’m letting the floor do all the lifting. Gravity is my teammate today..

sections.title: Rolling Smile
sections.tagline: A smile becomes powerful when it returns amplified.
body: Everyone stands or sits in a circle. The person who has the shortest hair begins by giving a big smile to one person of their choice. That person then smiles to someone else and the smile travels around, reaching each person and at the end needs to return to the starter.
Repeat new rounds with different challenges: Round 2: pass a high-five Round 3: pass a gentle shoulder tap Round 4: pass a quick hug (if comfortable)
If only two people participating, simply look at each other and smile for 30 seconds. Then if comfortable hug each other for another 30 seconds.
sections.note: Make your smile extra big - it travels better that way.

sections.title: The Quiet Hero
sections.tagline: Trust deepens when we honor silent kindness.
body: Each person names someone in the family
who often helps or supports others gently,
without drawing attention.
sections.note: Quiet heroes don’t brag - so it’s your job to shine a light on them.
